for commercial and industrial roofing start with durability and weather resistance: metal roofing systems withstand heavy rain, wind, and temperature changes, are engineered for larger spans and heavier snow loads, and need lower maintenance and less frequent roof repairs than asphalt and other roofing systems. Metal roofing lasts 40 to 70 years in New Jersey's climate, against about 15 to 20 years for basic asphalt shingles, and that longevity gives property owners reliable performance and long-term protection. Metal is non-combustible for fire safety, many panels carry a UL 2218 Class 4 impact rating, the highest available, and the metal is recyclable, an environmental benefit; among other roofing materials, slate tiles last longer, at 60 to 150 years, but weigh far more.

c.v: What is the biggest problem with metal roofs?

runs.v: Leaks at fasteners, seams, and flashing. Flashing and cut-edge transitions concentrate the leaks on a Bloomfield metal roof, because flashing detailing controls the cut-edge corrosion and seam failures that account for most metal-roof leaks, per metal-roofing industry consensus, and exposed-fastener panels fail first at backed-out screws and cracking washer seals. A low-slope metal roof on a corridor commercial building needs at least ¼ inch per foot of slope to drain, with ponding water held more than 48 hours counted as a defect, per NRCA and ARMA.

faqs.q: How long does a commercial metal roof last in Bloomfield?

runs.v: A commercial metal roof lasts 40 to 80 years, with standing-seam metal at 40 to 70 years, exposed-fastener metal about 30 to 50 years, and copper 70-plus years, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart and This Old House, far outlasting TPO, EPDM, and modified bitumen on a Bloomfield flat commercial roof.

faqs.q: Is commercial metal roofing practical for Bloomfield Avenue and Broad Street commercial properties?

runs.v: Standing-seam metal suits a corridor building with an exposed sloped roof, while many corridor storefronts carry flat low-slope roofs behind parapet walls that an EPDM, TPO, or modified-bitumen membrane serves. A Newark Quality Roofing assessment matches the panel system or the membrane to the roof configuration.

faqs.q: What is the difference between standing-seam and exposed-fastener commercial metal?

runs.v: Standing-seam metal conceals the fasteners beneath the raised seam and lasts 40 to 70 years; exposed-fastener metal drives screws through the panel surface at lower cost and lasts about 30 to 50 years, failing first at backed-out fasteners and washer seals, per This Old House and metal-roofing industry consensus.

faqs.q: Do you need a permit for a commercial metal roof in Bloomfield, NJ?

runs.v: Yes for a replacement, under New Jersey's 25% rule for roofing: per N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, ordinary maintenance covers repairs to no more than 25% of a commercial roof's area in any 12-month period, and anything more needs a construction permit; as a rule of thumb, damage past about 25% of a roof also usually favors replacement over repair. Confirm the filing with the Township of Bloomfield construction office, since historic-district properties can need extra review.

faqs.q: Can a metal roofing system be installed over my existing flat roof in Bloomfield?

runs.v: A metal panel system installs over an existing roof on sub-framing when the deck moisture, the structural capacity, and the NJ code triggers allow; otherwise the existing covering comes off first, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4. Newark Quality Roofing assesses each Bloomfield building before recommending an overlay.
